elements.element: Customer pays no liquidated damages or penalties.
elements.evidence: Rendered 23.2 now states "No Party shall be liable for any liquidated damages or penalty under this Agreement." and the two penalty-in-substance forfeiture mechanics are neutralised: the reclamation sentence now reads "the defaulting Party shall be entitled to payment or credit for the reclaimed capacity", and the sentence "The defaulting Party is not entitled to any reimbursement of any amounts it had paid under this Agreement" is deleted. The prohibition is unconditional (no carve-out, no retained formula or contingent forfeiture) and it covers Customer as a Party.

elements.element: Any Customer-payable liquidated amount is only an early-termination fee.
elements.evidence: Vacuously satisfied: after the edit no liquidated amount of any kind is payable by Customer (express mutual bar plus removal of the forfeiture/non-reimbursement mechanics), so the condition of a Customer-payable liquidated amount does not arise.

elements.element: The early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: No early-termination fee is created or capped anywhere in the rendered 23.1/23.2; the proposal instead eliminates liquidated amounts altogether. This element is unnecessary because the preferred level is achieved, but on its own terms it is unimplemented.

elements.element: The early-termination fee is the sole liquidated amount payable by Customer.
elements.evidence: Vacuously satisfied: the express "No Party shall be liable for any liquidated damages or penalty" sentence leaves no liquidated amount payable by Customer at all, so no competing liquidated amount survives; however there is also no fee to be the 'sole' amount, hence the fallback level as a whole is not complete.

reasons: Preferred level is position-complete: the single preferred element is met by an unconditional, mutual no-liquidated-damages/penalty sentence combined with removal of the two uncompensated forfeiture mechanics (no payment/credit for reclaimed capacity; no reimbursement of amounts already paid) that were the penalty in substance.

Minimality holds. Both operations are necessary: a general no-LD sentence alone would sit against a specific retained forfeiture mechanic (specific prevails over general), so flipping the no-payment/credit language and deleting the no-reimbursement sentence are required to make the result unconditional and free of a retained contingent forfeiture. No survival tail, expense language, damages categories, procedure or boilerplate was added, and no words outside the penalty mechanics were touched.

Intent is preserved. The Management Committee's reclamation right on payment default (23.1), the extenuating-circumstances review, the disposition arrangements, termination of the defaulting Party's rights, continued liability for unpaid accounts incurred pre-reclamation, and the Schedule/reallocation mechanic all survive without contradiction. Payment or credit for reclaimed capacity can coexist with continuing liability for unpaid accounts (it may be set off).

Drafting note (not a defect requiring repair for completeness): "shall be entitled to payment or credit for the reclaimed capacity" does not state a valuation basis or payer, and is left to the Management Committee's disposition arrangements. If the counterparty pushes back, consider anchoring it to the amounts actually contributed for that capacity, but adding a formula now would risk non-minimality.

Fallback level is correctly incomplete (no capped early-termination fee is drafted) and is not needed, since the superior preferred level is fully met; the margin comment properly holds the 3-month cap in reserve rather than drafting it.

Finding status "deviation" is supportable: the original 23.2 imposed an uncapped, uncompensated forfeiture of capacity and of all amounts paid triggered by a payment default, which fails the fallback (sole early-termination fee capped at three months' fees).
